day_shape: 85 items: UK announces additional military support to Saudi Arabia and G7 statement on Bab al-Mandab after renewed Houthi strikes, Iran floats seven-day Hormuz reopening tied to US easing pressure, heavy Khamenei school-year and Shabiri condolence messaging, Pezeshkian en route to UNGA.

threads.label: UK and G7 back Saudi against Houthis
threads.summary: The UK Ministry of Defence announced additional defensive military support to Saudi Arabia following renewed Houthi attacks, and G7 foreign ministers plus the EU issued a joint statement on Bab al-Mandab navigational rights. Sirens sounded on the Saudi-Yemen border, and the UNHRC said fighting has displaced more than 130,000 people in Yemen.

threads.label: Hormuz passage rules and reopening offer
threads.summary: A senior Iranian official told Reuters Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if the US eases military pressure and lifts its ports blockade, while an Iranian parliamentary committee approved a 20% cargo-seizure penalty for ships breaching Hormuz rules. Iran International reported a journalist tying June tanker attacks to oil-revenue middlemen, drawing treason accusations.

threads.label: Iran diplomacy around UNGA
threads.summary: Pezeshkian travelled to New York as Foreign Minister Araghchi accused Israel of a "free hand" on arrival and met EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas on the sidelines, per IRIB. Trump said he believed the US and Iran would reach a deal, while Iran International reported hardliners publicly discussing nuclear weapons and NPT withdrawal ahead of the trip.

threads.label: Khamenei academic-year messaging cycle
threads.summary: Khamenei's office released a message marking the reopening of schools and universities, with multiple excerpts pushed via Telegram on teachers, national identity, martyr students and "power from knowledge" against the "hegemonic system." Defa Press and IRIB amplified the message across the afternoon.

threads.label: Grand Ayatollah Shabiri Zanjani condolences
threads.summary: Khamenei's office issued a condolence message on the death of Grand Ayatollah Shabiri Zanjani, describing him as a "first-tier Shiite researcher" whose loss would take long to remedy. SNSC Secretary Mohsen Rezaei issued a parallel condolence message, per Defa Press.

threads.label: Sacred Defence Week programming
threads.summary: Defa Press pushed coverage of Sacred Defence Week including an IRGC Ground Forces motorised parade, army spokesman Amir Akraminia saying forces are "fully prepared to defend Iran," and Speaker Qalibaf visiting related exhibitions. A Council of Ministers decision set duties toward the Foundation for the Preservation of Sacred Defence Heritage.

threads.label: Gaza, UNGA speeches and Israeli threats
threads.summary: Defence Minister Israel Katz threatened to destroy remaining Gaza City and displace around a million Gazans if Hamas takes another hostage, while UN Secretary-General Guterres said Israel's offensive brought destruction "unlike anything" seen in his tenure. Regime channels amplified Qatari Emir Tamim and King of Jordan UNGA remarks condemning events in Gaza.

events.title_en: The loss of Grand Ayatollah Shabiri has created a gap among first-tier Shiite researchers
events.summary_en: The loss of Grand Ayatollah Shabiri has created a gap among first-tier Shiite researchers. Undoubtedly, the absence of this distinguished personality has created a gap among the ranks of first-tier Shiite researchers in the present age, the remedy of which may take a long time. I express condolences for this tragedy to our Master, may God hasten his return, the seminaries, and particularly the students, devotees and especially the esteemed household of this scholar and advocate of virtue, and I beseech God Almighty for the elevation of the ranks of this great man. From an excerpt of the Supreme Leader's message following the demise of Grand Ayatollah Shabiri, 31 Shahrivar 1405.

events.title_en: The presence of Grand Ayatollah Shabiri was a place of teaching and learning, and his conduct towards students and scholars was humble and paternal
events.summary_en: The presence of Grand Ayatollah Shabiri was a place of teaching and learning, and his conduct towards students and scholars was humble and paternal. By God's grace, for more than three decades now, many have had the privilege of benefiting from his presence to the extent of their capacity and to draw provisions for their scholarly gatherings and teaching. His presence was a place of teaching and learning, even when those attending would walk towards his home after the lesson. Apart from his established scholarly merit, his humble and paternal conduct towards students and scholars was also something observable and instructive. From an excerpt of the Supreme Leader's message following the demise of Grand Ayatollah Shabiri, 31 Shahrivar 1405.
